The given figure shows monthly changes in the human ovary during the reproductive cycle.

(The figure is a section of an ovary showing the clockwise ovarian cycle. Labelled structures: P and Q are developing/maturing follicles (the Graafian follicle is the large fluid-filled follicle on the right), T is the released ovum after ovulation, R is the corpus luteum (the large structure at the bottom formed after ovulation), and S is the degenerating corpus albicans on the left.)

Which of the following statements is correct regarding the labelled structures?
1. Before puberty, only structure T undergoes meiosis.
2. The hormone produced by structure R stimulates the pituitary gland to secrete luteinising hormone.
3. The hormone produced by structure S is responsible for the development of female secondary sex characters.
4. The hormone produced by P and Q stimulates the proliferation of the endometrial lining of the uterine wall.

A student decides to study the impact of removing certain flower parts on fruit formation in plant species X. He chooses three separate plants that are growing in the same plot under uniform conditions. The data is given in the table below.

| Plant | Part removed | Impact on formation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Anther | 30% less fruit formed than average plant in the plot |
| 2 | Stigma | No fruit formed |
| 3 | Petal | No significant impact |

Which of the following cannot be inferred from the above data?

options.label: A
options.text: Anthers and stigmas are crucial in sexual reproduction in species X.

options.label: B
options.text: Species X relies completely on cross-pollination.

options.label: C
options.text: Species X is likely to be wind-pollinated.

options.label: D
options.text: Pollen grains are probably unable to germinate if they land on other parts of the carpel besides the stigma.

New plants may be grown from groups of cells that are taken from other plants. The given diagram shows different parts of a plant X. Cell samples obtained from which of the labelled structures will grow into new plants genetically identical to plant X?

(The figure is a longitudinal section of a flower's carpel/pistil. Labelled parts: P is the anther at the top, Q is the style just below it, R points to the ovary which encloses a row of coiled ovules, and S points to the receptacle/base of the flower.)

In the given diagram the leaf shown belongs to which plant?

(The figure shows a single leaf lying flat, with several small plantlets bearing tiny roots and leaves growing from notches along the leaf margin. The plantlets are labelled "Adventitious buds".)

The diagram shows a section through the male reproductive system. What is the function of part X?

(The figure is a side-view section of the human male reproductive system showing the urinary bladder, the looping vas deferens, the urethra, the penis and the testis. Part X is labelled pointing to a gland (the prostate gland / accessory gland) lying just below the bladder where the vas deferens joins the urethra.)
1. The secretion of the gland neutralises acids from urine.
2. It decreases the number of sperms damaged during ejaculation.
3. It stimulates uterine contraction to help sperms move forward into the fallopian tube.
4. Both (i) and (ii)

The given diagram shows the carpel of an insect pollinated flower. What is the most likely reason for the non-germination of pollen grain Z?

(The figure is a carpel: a rounded ovary containing one ovule, a long style, and a stigma at the top. Two pollen grains labelled X and Y rest on the stigma surface, while pollen grain Z lies to the side, away from / not adhering to the stigma surface.)
1. Pollen grains X and Y were brought to the stigma earlier, therefore, their germination inhibited the germination of pollen grain Z.
2. Pollen grain Z was brought to the flower by wind, while pollen grains X and Y were brought to the flower by insects.
3. Pollen grain Z lacks protrusions that allow it to adhere properly onto the stigma surface.
4. Pollen grain Z comes from a flower of an incompatible species.

Which one of the following organism is represented by this diagram?

(The figure shows a fungus with a tangled mass of thread-like hyphae at the base from which several upright stalks rise, each ending in a rounded knob (sporangium). One sporangium on the right is bursting and releasing tiny dots labelled "Spores".)

Identify the mode of asexual reproduction in the following organism:

(The figure shows an organism with a tube-like body bearing several long thin tentacles at the top end, and a small outgrowth (bud) developing on the side of the body wall, which itself is forming tiny tentacles — i.e. a Hydra reproducing by budding.)
